report.answer_text:
Suzetrigine (Journavx) is a prescription, non-opioid pain pill that the FDA approved on January 30, 2025, for moderate to severe acute (short-term) pain in adults, including pain after surgery. (fda.gov)
It was notable because it was the first FDA-approved painkiller to selectively block NaV1.8, a sodium channel that helps peripheral sensory nerves transmit pain signals. Unlike opioids, it doesn’t act on opioid receptors. That gave clinicians a new way to treat acute pain without exposing patients to the risks of taking an opioid, such as addiction and overdose. (fda.gov)
In two post-surgery trials, suzetrigine relieved pain better than placebo, but it was not shown to outperform hydrocodone plus acetaminophen. Its approval was for acute pain, not chronic pain. (fda.gov)
